thread.title: Vance Reaffirms Full Confidence in Hegseth, Highlights Military Recruiting Trends
thread.title_full: Vance Reaffirms Full Confidence in Hegseth, Highlights Military Recruiting Trends

author: Smithy
text:
Are you joking?!?
1. Signal Chat Leaks (March 2025): Hegseth shared detailed operational plans for a U.S. airstrike on Houthi rebels in Yemen via a Signal group chat that inadvertently included The Atlantic editor-in-chief Jeffrey Goldberg. The chat, created by National Security Adviser Mike Waltz, contained specifics about targets, timing, and weapons (e.g., F-18s, drones, Tomahawk missiles).
2. Second Signal Chat Controversy (April 2025): Reports surfaced that Hegseth shared similar sensitive details about the same Yemen strikes in another Signal chat, this time with his wife, brother, lawyer, and others in a group called “Defense | Team Huddle.” This chat included flight schedules for F/A-18 aircraft, raising further concerns about his disregard for security protocols.
3. Leadership and Pentagon Chaos: Critics, including former Pentagon spokesperson John Ullyot, have described Hegseth’s tenure as chaotic, marked by internal strife and distractions from warfighting. Ullyot, despite supporting Hegseth, wrote in a Politico op-ed that the Pentagon was in “total chaos” after a “month from hell,” citing the Signal scandals, the firing of senior aides (e.g., Dan Caldwell, Darin Selnick) amid leak investigations, and Hegseth’s chief of staff resigning. Reports of Hegseth bringing his wife to sensitive meetings and the Pentagon’s focus on “endless drama” have fueled perceptions of dysfunction.
4. Perceived Incompetence and Lack of Qualifications: Hegseth faced skepticism during his confirmation due to his limited high-level military experience, lack of experience overseeing a large budget and large number of personnel, history of alcohol abuse, and allegations of sexual assault.
